title: Meromorphic module and the scalar map induced by a meromorphic section
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal M$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For an open $U$, let $\mathcal S(U)$ be the multiplicative subset of $\mathcal O_X(U)$ consisting of sections whose germ at each $x\in U$ is a non-zero-divisor in $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Define $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ as the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf $U\mapsto\mathcal S(U)^{-1}\mathcal M(U)$ with restriction $m/b\mapsto (m|_V)/(b|_V)$. Write $\mathcal K_X=\mathcal K_X(\mathcal O_X)$. The canonical map $\mathcal M\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ sends $m$ to $m/1$, and the canonical local fraction maps send $m/b$ to its sheafification image. For an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], this identifies $\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ with $\mathcal K_X\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal M$. A global meromorphic section $s$ is equivalently an $\mathcal O_X$-linear morphism $\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$; it induces the unique $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\mathcal K_X\to\mathcal K_X(\mathcal M)$ extending $s$, locally sending $a/b$ to $as/b$.
